provider.name: GitHub
provider.variantNote: Covers github.com. GitHub Enterprise Server has the same console under its own domain.

corrections: The first research pass treated OAuth Apps and GitHub Apps as one thing. They are two registrations with different token models; the guide covers both and says which GitHub recommends.
Marketplace listing requirements were first read as setup requirements. They apply only if you list, so they are facts here, not artifacts you must produce to go live.

scopeClasses.name: All scopes
scopeClasses.description: GitHub reviews nothing before external users can authorize an OAuth app or install a public GitHub App. The only gate you can hit is a customer's organization policy.

claims.text: You register an OAuth app from Settings, then Developer settings, then OAuth apps.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: In the left sidebar, click OAuth apps.

claims.text: The registration form asks for an application name.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: In "Application name", type the name of your app.

claims.text: A homepage URL for your app is a required field.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: In "Homepage URL", type the full URL to your app's website.

claims.text: An authorization callback URL is a required field.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: In "Authorization callback URL", type the callback URL of your app.

claims.text: An OAuth app can have up to 10 callback URLs.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: You can enter up to 10 callback URLs.

claims.text: A public GitHub App can be installed and authorized by any GitHub user, with no review by GitHub.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: If you set your GitHub App registration to public, any user on GitHub can install it and authorize it.

claims.text: A private GitHub App can only be installed on the owner's own account or organization.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: Private GitHub Apps can only be installed on the user or organization account of the app owner.

claims.text: Scopes are requested at authorization time as a space delimited list, not fixed at registration.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: A space-delimited list of scopes.

claims.text: Organization owners can restrict which OAuth apps reach their organization's repositories.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: Organizations can choose which OAuth apps have access to their repositories

claims.text: When an organization restricts OAuth apps, a member can request the owner's approval for yours.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: Users can request owner approval for OAuth apps they'd like to use

claims.text: Only if you list on the GitHub Marketplace: the listing needs a valid privacy policy link.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: Listings must have a valid link to a privacy policy.

claims.text: Only if you list on the GitHub Marketplace: the listing needs a support link.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: Listings must provide a method to receive support through a valid support link

claims.text: Paid Marketplace plans require the owning organization to be a verified publisher.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: your app must be owned by an organization that is a verified publisher.

claims.text: Paid Marketplace plans expect a GitHub App to have at least 100 installations.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: GitHub Apps should have a minimum of 100 installations.

claims.text: Paid Marketplace plans expect an OAuth app to have at least 200 users.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: OAuth apps should have a minimum of 200 users.

claims.text: Publisher verification requires two factor authentication on the organization.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: that you've enabled two-factor authentication for your organization

claims.text: Publisher verification requires a verified organization domain.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: that your organization's domain has been verified.

claims.text: Authenticated requests with a user token count against a limit of 5,000 requests per hour.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: All of these requests count towards your personal rate limit of 5,000 requests per hour.

claims.text: A GitHub App installation gets a minimum of 5,000 requests per hour.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: use the installation's minimum rate limit of 5,000 requests per hour.

claims.text: GitHub recommends GitHub Apps over OAuth apps.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: In general, GitHub Apps are preferred over OAuth apps.

claims.text: GitHub App installation tokens expire after one hour, so plan token refresh from the start.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: Installation access tokens expire after a predefined amount of time (currently 1 hour).

claims.text: A user sent to the authorize endpoint with an unregistered client_id sees GitHub's sign in page first; the client is checked only after sign in, so a wrong client ID looks like a normal login to your users until the error appears.
claims.label: tested

probes.summary: An unregistered client_id gets GitHub's sign in page (title: Sign in to GitHub) before any client check.
No OpenID discovery document at github.com; the authorize and token endpoints come from the docs.
Probe could not run: github.com disallows automated fetching of /settings/developers (robots).

steps.title: Decide between an OAuth app and a GitHub App
steps.detail: GitHub recommends GitHub Apps: fine grained permissions and one hour installation tokens. Pick an OAuth app only when you need a plain user token flow.
inputs: Whether you act on behalf of users or on repositories

steps.title: Sign in to GitHub and open Settings, Developer settings, OAuth apps
inputs: A GitHub account; an organization account if the app should be owned by the org

steps.title: Register the app with a name, a homepage URL and your callback URLs
steps.detail: Up to 10 callback URLs. Use the redirect URI from your Composio auth config.

steps.title: Generate the client secret and store the client ID and secret in your auth config
inputs: A place to keep the secret

steps.title: Choose the scopes you request at authorization time
steps.detail: Scopes are a space delimited list in the authorize request. Request the least you need; organizations review scope use when approving apps.

steps.title: Ship. Any GitHub user can authorize the app now
steps.detail: For a GitHub App, set it to public so any account can install it. There is no GitHub review before external users connect.

steps.title: Plan for organization approvals
steps.detail: Customers whose organizations restrict OAuth apps will need an owner to approve yours. Give users the request flow and keep the scope list small.
inputs: A short note for customers' org owners

steps.title: Only if you list on the Marketplace: publish a privacy policy and a support link, and get publisher verification for paid plans
steps.detail: Listing is optional. Paid plans expect 100 installations (GitHub App) or 200 users (OAuth app) and a verified publisher organization with 2FA and a verified domain.

playbooks.symptom: A user in a company account authorizes the app but it cannot see their organization's repositories.
playbooks.cause: The organization restricts OAuth app access and your app has not been approved by an owner.
playbooks.fix: Ask the user to request owner approval from the authorization page, or have an organization owner approve the app under the organization's third party access settings.

playbooks.symptom: Users report hitting rate limits after your app grows.
playbooks.cause: User tokens share the user's 5,000 requests per hour. Installation tokens get their own 5,000 minimum.
playbooks.fix: Move to a GitHub App so each installation has its own limit, and cache or use conditional requests.

playbooks.symptom: Users see a GitHub sign in page and then an error after signing in.
playbooks.cause: The client_id in your authorize URL is wrong or the callback URL is not one of the registered ones. GitHub checks the client after sign in.
playbooks.fix: Compare the client_id and redirect_uri in the authorize request with the app registration. Up to 10 callback URLs can be registered.
